nodes.line: Sit down if you like. Nobody else is using it.

I'll be straight with you. The Gosford order has been two cartons light every week since a public holiday nobody remembered and the invoice says otherwise every time. It has been going on longer than I have admitted to anyone. You'll know it when you see it.

It has been three weeks. They admitted it, which I did not expect, so now there is $32 owing to Gosford and it is not going to walk in here itself. I have got no proof, which is exactly why I am asking. Half now if you want it. Most people don't.
Right. Tell me and do not soften it.

choices.text: The Credit Note, Gosford — that's done.

nodes.line: Right you are. Mind the step.
You will have to speak up, the trains are in.

Nobody else has offered, so. I do the Gosford run at just gone midnight and there is a stretch of it where the van gets followed, which I have told nobody until now. It might be nothing. It has not felt like nothing. Whatever it costs you, tell me and I will cover it.

The council knows and the council does not care. I have got an esky with no lid in the back of the van and the Gosford shop is shut, and the number on the door rings out. I would not ask if there was anyone else about. I would rather know than wonder.
I have been thinking about it all day. Out with it.
Fair enough. You know where I am.

npcs.name: Ava, the kid on the register at Gosford

nodes.line: I have got about four minutes before I am needed.

I have been putting it off since Easter. Three of the Gosford regulars have started coming in together and going out separately, and the till is $18 down on those days. You can tell me I am imagining it. Tell me after. That's the whole job. No catch.

Before you say anything: yes, I know. Everything Gosford sells comes off a floor at Point Clare, and the woman who runs it will tell you things she will not put in writing. I would have sorted it myself a year ago. Be polite about it. It costs nothing.
Well? I can read your face from here.
Suit yourself. The offer does not go anywhere.

npcs.name: Tayla, junior coach at Beverly Hills

nodes.line: Ah. Someone with two working legs.

I'll be straight with you. I have got eleven kids for a twelve-a-side at Beverly Hills on Thursdays and one of them has a note from his mother. It has been going on longer than I have admitted to anyone. You'll know it when you see it.

It has been three weeks. We found a twelfth, which means the Beverly Hills club now owes the association $49 it had budgeted on not owing. I have got no proof, which is exactly why I am asking. Half now if you want it. Most people don't.
Sit. Talk. Then I will decide how I feel.

nodes.line: You are early. Or late. I have lost track.

Nobody else has offered, so. The canteen at Beverly Hills does two hundred sausages on a Saturday and this week the freezer went off at two in the afternoon. It might be nothing. It has not felt like nothing. Whatever it costs you, tell me and I will cover it.

The council knows and the council does not care. Somebody walked off with the float from the Beverly Hills canteen at about two in the afternoon during the last home game, and I have a fair idea which somebody. I would not ask if there was anyone else about. I would rather know than wonder.
You have got that look. Good or bad, out with it.

I'll be straight with you. Somebody has been tipping fill into the creek behind Turramurra since the first of the month and it is narrowing the channel a metre at a time. It has been going on longer than I have admitted to anyone. You'll know it when you see it.

It has been three weeks. They have agreed to a clean-up at Turramurra, which is wonderful, except the grant is $59 short and closes on the first of the month. I have got no proof, which is exactly why I am asking. Half now if you want it. Most people don't.
Alright. I am listening properly this time.

choices.text: The Creek Behind Turramurra — that's done.

nodes.line: Suit yourself. The offer does not go anywhere.
If you are selling something the answer is no.

Nobody else has offered, so. We had 26 sandbags in the Turramurra shed on the first of the month and this morning we have got the pallet they came on. It might be nothing. It has not felt like nothing. Whatever it costs you, tell me and I will cover it.

The council knows and the council does not care. People keep driving the low crossing at Turramurra at first light with the water over the sign, and one of them is going to be the one. I would not ask if there was anyone else about. I would rather know than wonder.
Say it plain and I will pay you plain.

choices.text: The Low Crossing, Turramurra — that's done.

npcs.name: Isla, resident who got flooded at Turramurra

nodes.line: Cash only and no, I am joking. What do you want.

I have been putting it off since Easter. The water came through my place at Turramurra on the first of the month and the assessor wants photographs of things I have already thrown out. You can tell me I am imagining it. Tell me after. That's the whole job. No catch.

Before you say anything: yes, I know. Whatever is happening to Turramurra starts upstream at Warrawee, and there are people up there who have been saying so for years. I would have sorted it myself a year ago. Be polite about it. It costs nothing.
I had a feeling. Go on.

choices.text: Under the House, Turramurra — that's done.
